title: Profit, loss and discount: practice set
sourceNote: Original practice questions written for this group. None of them is a CAT previous-year question.
instructions: 10 questions, 20 minutes, CAT marking: +3 right, -1 wrong multiple choice, 0 for a wrong type-in answer.
Type-in answers take a number only: no %, ₹ or units. Use a decimal, not a fraction.

questions.text: An article bought for ₹250 is sold for ₹300. What is the profit percentage?
An article is sold for ₹990 at a loss of 10%. What was its cost price (in ₹)?
The marked price of a shirt is ₹800 and the shop gives a 15% discount. What is the selling price?
A trader marks his goods 40% above cost price and then allows a 10% discount. What is his profit percentage?
A jacket has a marked price of ₹1,500. Two successive discounts of 20% and 10% are given. What is the selling price?
A shopkeeper sells an article at a profit of 12%. Had he sold it for ₹24 more, his profit would have been 20%. What is the cost price (in ₹)?
By what percentage above cost price must a shopkeeper mark an article so that, after allowing a 20% discount, he still makes a profit of 20%?
A dealer sells two articles for ₹1,200 each. On one he makes a profit of 20% and on the other a loss of 20%. His overall result is
A shopkeeper sells at 10% above his cost price per kg but gives only 900 g when a customer pays for 1 kg. What is his actual profit percentage?
A trader buys 50 kg of rice at ₹40 per kg. During storage 20% of the rice is spoiled and cannot be sold. At what price per kg (in ₹) must he sell the rest to make an overall profit of 17.5%?
